analysis.title: "What Happens When The Music Stops?" BTIG Warns Of A Correlation-One Selloff As Semis Can't Find A Bottom
key_insights: BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky says the market has rotated between cohorts without net progress. In late September 18% of SPX names were oversold, RSP was 7% off highs near its 200 DMA, and SOXX had rallied nearly 20%. Now semis are oversold and RSP is back at highs.

On Wednesday 22% of S&P 500 components closed with a 14-day RSI above 70 while the index RSI was 50.4. Krinsky says this is the second-lowest SPX RSI ever with more than 22% of components overbought. Only April 19, 1999 was more extreme.

Prior analogs started with a high-single-digit drawdown but diverged after. April 1999: S&P fell about 9% into October 1999, then rallied about 26% into the March 2000 high. February 11, 2026: 23% of names overbought with index RSI 52.5, followed by a decline of about 10% into the March lows.

SOXX is down 14% in five days and gapped lower again at the open. Semis broke their July lows with no downside exhaustion signals, and Krinsky sees big-picture downside risk even though a counter-trend bounce is likely due soon.
XLV is 19% above its 200-day moving average, the widest spread on record going back to the late 1990s. Staples, utilities and healthcare have been the destination for money leaving semis.

Krinsky's correlation-one selloff condition: semis cannot bounce and overbought defensives begin to correct. His base case if semis stabilize is another rotation, with overbought areas correcting and money returning to chips.

Goldman's Japan Semiconductors basket fell 12% overnight and is down 22% over five days. It was up 100% at the end of June and is now up 27%. Krinsky says it looks more like a meaningful top. The basket now sits on its early-2026 support shelf after the uptrend from the April 2025 low broke in the summer.

The Nasdaq outperformed the SOX by nearly 460bps on Wednesday. Goldman's derivatives desk says the spread between its hyperscaler and data-center/semis baskets was the second-largest on record, behind only DeepSeek Monday.

Wednesday's Dow gain of 3%+ while closing within 3% of a 52-week high was only the third such day in 30 years. The other two were Nov 6, 2024 and May 16, 2001, and both saw meaningful weakness over the following six months. Krinsky calls the stat statistically irrelevant.

Goldman's CTA model sees $164 billion of S&P supply in a down-tape, after hedges were sold in one of the biggest vol crushes in two decades. Goldman's Rich Privorotsky argues nets are too low for the broader market to go down easily.

Bloomberg's Alyce Andres says the S&P e-mini selloff at the open, about 150 points in roughly 35 minutes, bears the hallmarks of programmatic selling. TD Securities strategists say CTA sales likely triggered as the contract slid through 7665. Volume was above a million contracts, elevated for the time of day.

The article author's own take is that the rotation story explained why the S&P went nowhere for three months, but with XLV at a record stretch it is hard to see where the next defensive buying comes from. The author sees a correlation-one selloff as more likely than another lap of rotation.

tension_points.bull_case: If semis stabilize, Krinsky's base case is another rotation where overbought areas correct and money returns to chips. Goldman's Privorotsky says nets are too low for the broader market to go down easily.
tension_points.bear_case: If semis cannot bounce while overbought defensives begin to correct, everything falls together. Krinsky points to semis breaking July lows with no exhaustion signal, XLV 19% above its 200DMA, and Goldman's CTA model showing $164 billion of S&P supply in a down-tape.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A semis bounce, which Krinsky says is likely due soon, would support the rotation case. A failure to bounce, with oversold names unable to rally while overbought names correct, triggers the correlation-one selloff.

theme_stances.key_argument: If oversold semis cannot bounce and overbought defensives begin to correct, the market faces a correlation-one selloff.
theme_stances.evidence: That is the condition for the correlation-one selloff
